Resolves #9075

Grid column selection never repainted its cells. `grid.Row` paints the column class when it creates its content, and `grid.Body#createViewData` skips every row whose record and index are unchanged. So the unforced re-projection each column model ran after changing `selectedColumns` reached nothing: not on select, not on arrow navigation, not on clear. The three copies of that logic had also drifted apart. `ColumnModel#onCellClick` returned early on every click, and `CellColumnModel` could never clear a column with a second click. Column selection now lives once in `BaseModel`, and the three models call it: `setSelectedColumns`, a granular `updateColumns` that is the column counterpart to #9014's `updateRows`, and `stepSelectedColumn`. Swapping a row- or column-selecting model out no longer leaves its highlight painted.

Review R1 found two more defects, both fixed here:
- **Integer keys.** A real cell click delivers its record id as a dataset string. `Body#getRecord` looked it up as given, so an integer-keyed store resolved no record and every cell model ignored the click. It now gives an integer-keyed store its number back, which replaces `getRecordFromLogicalId`'s `parseInt` copy.
- **Row flush.** The removed re-projection had been flushing `CellRowModel`'s silent row write in every body. `CellColumnRowModel` now flushes the clicked record's row in each body itself.

This narrows #9075 per @tobiu's option A; the rest of #9075 moved to **#18707** ([scope comment](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/9075#issuecomment-5669650030)).

Evidence: L2 (unit arms over a real grid, asserting painted cell classes and the rendered row vnode across three bodies; red-first, with each R1 fix reverted alone to prove its own arm) → L2 required. Residual: none.

## Deltas from ticket

**#9075 is narrowed, and two of its mechanisms were reshaped, not implemented.**
- **No mixins.** Neo mixins assign over a class's own methods, and a copied method keeps its home object (`Neo.mjs:1184`), so `super` breaks. The column methods `super`-chain, so shared helpers on `BaseModel` host them instead.
- **No polymorphic `updateItem`.** Replacing the `includes('__')` branch with a per-class `updateItem` does not fit, because one `CellRowModel` feeds both record ids and cell ids through `updateBodyRows`.

Both, plus the row-selection trait #18626 deferred and the ID objective, are in #18707.

**Two R1 fixes reach past column selection.** `Body#getRecord` is the shared record lookup for grid cell and row events. `CellColumnRowModel`'s row flush restores what the removed re-projection did by accident. `CellRowModel`'s own split-row flush is unchanged and stays with #9492.

**The row swap-out fix is in scope** although #9075 is about columns. It is the same flaw — an unforced re-projection in the same method — proven red first, and leaving it would have meant knowingly shipping it in a method this PR rewrites.

**`ViewOwnedSelectionModel.spec.mjs` "a column-selecting model swaps out cleanly" was rewritten.** It asserted that every body re-projected on swap-out: the call that repainted nothing, which is this ticket's defect. It now asserts the contract — no throw, and no body keeps a column painted — with one selected column per body. A row counterpart was added beside it.

**Arrow navigation reads the column selection's own state.** `stepSelectedColumn` starts from `selectedColumns[0]`, or the first column when none is selected. `ColumnModel` already did; the Cell\* copies consulted `hasSelection()`, which is the *cell* selection there. The two only disagree when a cell is selected without its column, or the reverse — a state a click cannot produce.

`unregister` skips the repaint while the view is being destroyed, mirroring `Model#unregister`: a dying grid has nothing left to paint, and its bodies' stores may already be gone.

## Test Evidence

**Red-first against unchanged source.** I stashed only the five source files and ran the specs; the control was `git diff --stat`. That first run, with the original numeric fixture, gave 11 failed, 12 passed:
- `ColumnModel`: the click selected nothing.
- `CellColumnModel` and `CellColumnRowModel`: `selectedColumns` was set but no cell was painted.
- The row swap-out arm: row 1 stayed painted.
- The column swap-out arm: `setSelectedColumns` did not exist yet. That arm guards the new path, not the old defect.

An earlier attempt was void, because zsh passed a space-joined path variable to `git stash` as a single pathspec.

**R1, red at `ce1c783390`.**
- The browser-shaped fixture reddens all six `CellColumnModel` and `CellColumnRowModel` arms. `ColumnModel` needs no record and stays green.
- The new click arm fails at "CellModel selects the clicked cell".
- The row arm, with string business keys, fails on the move: `[['r2'], ['r2'], []]`.

**Each R1 fix reverted alone.**
- Without the flush, only the row arm fails: 1 failed, 15 passed.
- Without the resolver, only the seven integer-key arms fail: 7 failed, 18 passed.

**A limit of the row arm.** In the unit harness the first click still renders the row in all three bodies at `ce1c783390`. Counting calls showed no row or body update reaching start or end, yet their rows re-rendered through the selection flow's `view.update()`. On the move that no longer holds, and the end body stays empty, as in the reviewer's browser matrix. So the move is where the arm discriminates.

### 🔬 Depth Floor
**Challenge:** All six grid models were checked. The two blocking findings are:

**1. [P2] Preserve the combined model's row flush when replacing column re-projection.**  
In `CellColumnRowModel#onCellClick`, the new `setSelectedColumns` call updates rows only in bodies whose column cells changed. Its superclass `CellRowModel#onCellClick` subsequently calls `selectRow(recordId, true)`: every body's row VDOM changes silently, and the cell selection flush reaches the clicked body.

Fresh browser grids, string business keys `r1/r2/r3`, `useInternalId:false`, and three columns split start/center/end; click `r1/col2`. After 600 ms:

| Revision | Selected row in VDOM, start/center/end | Selected row in actual DOM |
|---|---|---|
| parent `d8e13f46d0` | `[[r1],[r1],[r1]]` | `[[r1],[r1],[r1]]` |
| head `ce1c783390` | `[[r1],[r1],[r1]]` | `[[],[r1],[]]` |

A subsequent click on `r2/col3` leaves head DOM rows `[[],[r2],[r2]]`, versus all three on the parent. The old unforced column call failed to construct column classes, but its body update also flushed pending row changes. Removing it regresses this combined model. A VDOM-class-only assertion passes both revisions and misses the regression.

**2. [P2] The new numeric-key click tests do not reproduce a browser click.**  
`ColumnSelection.spec.mjs:94–100` passes numeric `recordId` directly into the event path. The browser supplies a string. With the spec's same Integer key / `useInternalId:false` combination, an actual click delivers `data.field="col2"`, `data.recordId="1"`; `Body#fireCellEvent` resolves no record. All four cell-based models receive `record:undefined` and select nothing; ColumnModel and RowModel are positive controls that do select. Changing only the business keys to strings makes the cell models select.

The resolver defect predates this PR. However, the changed `CellColumnModel:39` now additionally gates its column state on that unresolved record: parent click sets `selectedColumns=["col2"]`, head leaves `[]`. The PR's advertised click repair and new tests need the real boundary, rather than certifying the numeric shortcut.

**Family coverage:** ColumnModel, CellColumnModel and CellColumnRowModel receive the new column helper. RowModel and CellRowModel inherit the new row cleanup; CellModel retains its inherited cell cleanup. With string-key positive controls, actual DOM selection clears on swap to `null` for **all six**, across all three bodies. Parent row/combined-row controls retain stale rows. No separate copy of this cleanup is needed in the untouched models.
